configuration.load_balance_note: Uniform spatial particle initialization across z assigns approximately N_p / size particles to each equal-height slab and represents the best-case scenario for parallel load balance.
configuration.profiled_stage_note: Per-stage breakdown timings are measured in a separate profiled pass (ps.profile=True, solver._profile_mpi=True). Per-stage cudaStreamSynchronize() barriers inflate stage times relative to the unprofiled coupled step median, and for MPI runs (size > 1) each stage is reduced as the maximum over ranks (MPI.MAX) and then summed across stages (sum_s max_r t_{r,s} >= max_r sum_s t_{r,s}), which is why the 2-GPU stage sum can exceed the profiled step total.
configuration.baseline_and_efficiency_note: The library default is periodic cell sorting sort_every=50; headline 2-GPU speedup (b) compares 2 L4 NCCL against 1 L4 with sort_every=50 (pre-sorted after warm-up and timed over >= sort_every steps per repeat so amortised sort cost is included). Speedup (a) compares unsorted runs (sort_every=0). Parallel efficiency (c) is defined against the equal-work 1-L4 half-domain N_p/2 control (t_half_ctrl / t_2gpu), isolating communication and migration overhead from single-GPU domain-size effects; apparent efficiency against the full-domain 1-L4 baseline ((t_1gpu / t_2gpu) / 2) is reported separately.

working_set_sweep.rise_onset_criterion: first interval i such that every later jump from i onward is > -l2_step_noise_factor_k * noise_within_sweep_ns_per_particle and the jump at i is > +l2_step_noise_factor_k * noise_within_sweep_ns_per_particle

caption: At N_p = 10,000,000, the headline 2-GPU NCCL speedup at the library default (periodic cell sorting sort_every=50, amortised sort cost included) is (b) 1.8x (two-run min-max 1.8x-1.8x) (sorted push+deposit 4.9 vs 5.0 ns/particle; sort call 21 ms / 1% amortised share on 1 L4 and 10 ms / 1% on 2 L4), compared with (a) 2.0x (two-run min-max 2.0x-2.0x) with NCCL and 2.0x (two-run min-max 2.0x-2.0x) with pinned-host MPI against the unsorted 1-L4 baseline (sort_every=0), and (c) parallel efficiency vs the equal-work 1-L4 64x64x64 N_p/2 half-domain control (t_half_ctrl / t_2gpu) is 88% (two-run min-max 87%-88%) (whereas apparent efficiency (t_1gpu / t_2gpu) / 2 against the full-domain unsorted 1-L4 baseline is 102%). At N_p = 10,000,000, unsorted per-particle push+deposit changes by -12% on 2 GPUs (5.4 vs 6.1 ns/particle on 1 L4) and by -15% (5.2 ns/particle) on the 1-L4 64x64x64 N_p/2 half-domain control. In the 1-L4 fixed-density working-set sweep (nz = 16..256, push+deposit kernel working set 5.0..75.8 MB and total field+current working set 15.0..227.4 MB vs 50.3 MB L2 cache), unsorted push+deposit starts at 5.4 ns/particle (nz=16, push+deposit kernel working set 5.0 MB, total field+current working set 15.0 MB) and rises to 8.5 ns/particle (nz=256, push+deposit kernel working set 75.8 MB, total field+current working set 227.4 MB): under the noise-aware rise-onset rule (first interval i with jump > +k·noise_within_sweep and all jumps from i onward > -k·noise_within_sweep, using unsorted within-sweep noise (max of 2 back-to-back pairs) = 0.016 ns/particle, k=3.0, threshold 0.049 ns/particle), the sustained rise is gradual, beginning in the push+deposit kernel working-set interval 19.2..28.6 MB (nz=64..96, total field+current working set 57.5..85.8 MB), and no discrete step at the 50.3 MB L2 cache size is resolved because across the L2-bracketing push+deposit kernel working-set interval the jump exceeds k=3.0 times the unsorted within-sweep noise (max of 2 back-to-back pairs) (0.016 ns/particle, threshold 0.049 ns/particle) but does not exceed the jumps implied by the two neighbouring intervals' slopes per log working set — the jump exceeds the noise (unsorted within-sweep noise, max of 2 back-to-back pairs) but not the trend (unsorted within-sweep noise is 0.016 ns/particle, max of 2 back-to-back pairs — the back-to-back estimate rests on 2 pairs; the median repeat span is 0.17 ns/particle — vs unsorted cross-phase offset 0.29 ns/particle, max of 2 cross-phase pairs against the 1-L4 baseline and half-domain control, so the two noise classes differ by 18x) (across the L2-bracketing push+deposit kernel working-set interval 38.0..56.9 MB the jump is 0.74 ns/particle vs 0.79 ns/particle from lower neighbour, 2.0 ns/particle from upper neighbour implied by neighbour log-slopes; across the L2-bracketing total field+current working-set interval 43.4..57.5 MB the change is -0.10 ns/particle). By contrast, over the rising regime (push+deposit kernel working set 19.2..75.8 MB, total field+current working set 57.5..227.4 MB), the cell-sorted curve (sort_every=50) rises 5.7% (5.1 to 5.4 ns/particle, span 0.29 ns/particle > sorted within-sweep k·noise = 0.030 ns/particle, where k=3.0 times sorted within-sweep noise 0.010 ns/particle, max of 2 sorted back-to-back pairs; for sorted, the back-to-back estimate rests on 2 pairs; the median repeat span is 0.060 ns/particle) vs unsorted 55% (span 3.0 ns/particle), so the sorted curve is not flat within sorted within-sweep k·noise (max of 2 sorted back-to-back pairs) but its rise is much smaller (9.7x smaller in relative rise, 11x smaller in span; over the full sweep sorted rises 17% from 4.6 to 5.4 ns/particle vs unsorted 58%), demonstrating that the unsorted penalty is locality-dependent and consistent with an L2 cache-residency effect as a stated hypothesis. Two-GPU execution pays 12% (two-run min-max 12%-15%) of the profiled stage sum (12% (two-run min-max 12%-17%) of the unprofiled step median) in particle migration and compaction. In the separate profiled pass, each stage time is reduced as the maximum over MPI ranks and then summed across stages, which is why the 2-GPU stage sum can exceed the profiled step total. All 16 sorted controls passed the unsorted-referenced profiling consistency check (|t_prof_s - t_med_s| <= |t_prof_u - t_med_u| + jitter_u). Electromagnetic FIT field updates (B + E advance) are ~2% of the 1-GPU profiled stage sum at N_p = 10,000,000 (<= 17% across N_p >= 10^6), so the field solver's own scaling is not tested in the particle-dominated regime. At N_p = 100,000 (field- and communication-latency-bound), the 2-GPU speedups vs unsorted 1 L4 are 1.5x with NCCL and 1.1x with pinned-host MPI. Run-to-run relative spread between the two independent cloud VMs is at most 1.6% over the N_p = 10,000,000 speedup and efficiency quantities (1.6% including the N_p = 100,000 speedups), and 30% relative (<=4.3 percentage points) on the N_p = 10,000,000 2-GPU migration share; cross-VM per-nz working-set offset (repeat minus primary, not pooled into k·noise) has mean +0.06 ns/particle (max |diff| 0.13 ns/particle, 8/8 same sign) on unsorted and +0.06 ns/particle (max |diff| 0.098 ns/particle, 8/8 same sign) on sorted push+deposit, which is smaller than the unsorted cross-phase offset (0.29 ns/particle, max of 2 cross-phase pairs); quoted values are from the primary run, with two-run min-max ranges shown in parentheses. Comparing 2 GPUs against 1 GPU on a single node measures a 2-GPU speedup, not a multi-rank strong-scaling curve.
